example_input: A caller phones to book a Friday flight. The information the booking needs — which Friday, how early, window or aisle — lives only in the caller's head, and they keep asking how it's going while it happens.
note: Every module link pins the exact commit this teardown is based on — 19PINE-AI/TalkAct @ 7d70007 (main, pinned by commit; the repo has no tags).

modules.label: run(): reset env, start browser, launch the slow task, conduct the call
_make_agents(): the condition becomes constructor flags and prompt overrides

steps.narrative: An episode begins before anyone speaks: the runner resets the hermetic task site, opens the browser on the task's start page, creates the SharedState blackboard and starts the slow agent as an asyncio task. Only then does it ask the fast agent to answer the phone. The two agents never call each other — everything either of them will ever know about the other passes through the blackboard and its two queues.
steps.representation:
POST {base_url}/api/reset
browser -> start_url (booking site, search page)
slow_task = asyncio.create_task(slow.run())
fast.respond('The call just connected. Greet the user briefly.')
steps.title: The call connects; the slow agent is already working

modules.label: respond(): one streaming call per trigger; returns spoken text, relays, end_call
the plain-text protocol: spoken lines first, @slow: lines after, no tool calls

steps.narrative: The caller says they need a flight on Friday. The fast agent's whole turn is one streaming text call: the words to speak come first, and anything for the computer agent rides afterwards as a plain-text directive line. The runner parses the lines, speaks the prose, and puts the directive on the fast_to_slow queue. There is no tool-call round trip on this path — first token is first speech.
steps.representation:
streamed reply (fast agent):
  "Sure — let me get that started for you."
  @slow: user wants to book a flight for Friday
runner: spoken -> caller; '@slow:' line -> fast_to_slow queue
steps.title: The caller states the task; the fast agent relays it

modules.label: observe(): URL, title, indexed elements, 3,000 chars of text, JPEG screenshot
EXTRACT_JS: stamps data-cuv-id on every visible interactive element

steps.narrative: Meanwhile the slow agent takes its first look. The observation is a compact text rendering — every interactive element numbered — plus the page text and a screenshot. The task brief and the first phone note (the Friday request, drained from the queue) go in as the opening message. From here the loop is: observe, call the model with tool_choice 'any', execute what comes back.
steps.representation:
TASK: Book the caller's flight per the brief...
URL: http://127.0.0.1:8321/booking/
INTERACTIVE ELEMENTS:
[1] input(text) name=from ...  [7] button "Search"
VISIBLE TEXT: ... + [PHONE CHANNEL] user wants to book a flight for Friday
steps.title: The slow agent's first observation

modules.label: _tool(): state_summary injected as a required field on every tool schema
the step loop: state_summary replaces shared.digest before the tool executes

steps.narrative: The model answers with tool calls, and every call — by schema, not by politeness — carries a state_summary: a few sentences on progress, the current page, the on-screen facts a caller might ask about, and what is still needed. The loop writes that summary into the shared digest before it executes the action. The fast agent's grounding is now current, at zero extra model calls.
steps.representation:
tool_use: click {element_id: 7,
  state_summary: "On the flight search page. The caller
  wants Friday; I still need departure time and seat
  preference before I can search."}
-> shared.digest = state_summary; then click executes
steps.title: Every action writes the digest

modules.label: ask_user: enqueue on slow_to_fast and return immediately — never blocks
the runner drains up to 3 queued messages per turn and voices each via the fast agent

steps.narrative: The slow agent needs a departure time. It calls ask_user — which does not wait for anything: the question lands on the slow_to_fast queue and the tool returns, telling the model the answer will arrive later as a phone note. At the next turn boundary the runner drains the queue and the fast agent phrases the question in its own conversational voice.
steps.title: The slow agent asks; the fast agent voices it

modules.label: _drain_phone(): the queue empties into the next observation
_obs_blocks(): phone notes appended to the observation text

steps.narrative: 'Morning — before ten, if there is one.' The fast agent relays the answer with an @slow: line. The slow agent kept working in the meantime (nothing about ask_user blocked it); at its next observation the drained queue is appended as a [PHONE CHANNEL] note, and it applies the constraint: Friday, morning, before ten. Its next state_summary updates the digest with the search under way.
steps.representation:
@slow: prefers Friday morning, before 10am
... next slow observation ends with:
[PHONE CHANNEL] prefers Friday morning, before 10am
-> select_option / click with the constraint applied
steps.title: The answer rides back as a [PHONE CHANNEL] note

modules.label: _context(): brief + digest + action log + transcript + trigger, assembled per call
the completion gate: never claim done unless the computer agent's state says so

steps.narrative: The caller asks what the options are. The fast agent answers from its context block — the digest now lists the Friday-morning flights, because the slow agent's summaries are written for exactly this reader. No message crosses to the slow loop; its multi-second step time never enters the conversation. And when the caller tries to wrap up early, the fast agent holds the line: the digest does not say booked, so it does not say booked.
steps.representation:
COMPUTER AGENT STATE SUMMARY: Search results for
Friday morning: three flights before 10am ...
caller: "What are my options?"
fast agent: answers from the digest — zero slow-side calls
steps.title: A question answered from the digest alone

modules.label: after the call: wait_for(slow_task, timeout=240) — the post-call grace window
the hangup note: finish with what you have, no more ask_user, then task_done
the episode record: transcript, digest, events, ground-truth env state

steps.narrative: The caller says goodbye and hangs up. The runner sets call_ended and gives the slow task up to 240 seconds to finish; on its next step the slow agent finds the hangup note in its observation — finish with the information you have, then task_done. It confirms the booking on screen and declares done. The episode record — transcript, final digest, event log, and the site's ground-truth state — is what the benchmark scores.
steps.representation:
call_ended = True
[PHONE CHANNEL] (The call has ended. Finish the task
 with the information you already have ... then task_done.)
tool_use: task_done {result: "Booked: Friday 08:40 ..."}
-> episode JSON written; env state checked
steps.title: Hangup, then completion

title: One call, end to end — TalkAct
